title: Normalized integral immersion pullbacks over completed coefficients
statement:
Fix the global datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Put $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$, $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ on the small pro-etale site of $T=X,U,Z$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $\mathcal C_T=D^b_c(T,R)$ for the full derived-complete integral constructible subcategory of $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_T))$, with uniformly bounded constructible finite reductions [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed].

The schemes $X,U,Z$ are Noetherian and qcqs, $j$ is quasi-compact, and $(R,(t))$ has finite perfect quotients, with finite free resolutions $[R\xrightarrow{t^n}R]$. The canonical coefficient maps $g^{-1}B_X\xrightarrow{\sim}B_Y$, for $g=i,j$ and $Y=Z,U$, preserve constant $R$-sections, quotient projections and quotient transitions [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image].

Let $g_o^*$ be ordinary module inverse image along these coefficient identifications [def-sf-proetale-ring-sheaf-operations], let $g_c^*$ be the strict quotient-tower completed pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and let $g_R^*$ be the specified integral pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. There are natural isomorphisms of functors on $\mathcal C_X$
$$g_R^*\xrightarrow{\gamma_g}g_c^*\xleftarrow{c_g}g_o^*.$$
Here $\gamma_g$ identifies the defining strict-tower projection maps, and $c_g$ is the actual completion comparison. Both respect finite quotient projections, quotient transitions and shifts. The composite $c_g^{-1}\gamma_g$ identifies the specified integral pullback with ordinary termwise inverse image, including its canonical shift comparison. These functors are exact and $R$-linear, preserve derived completeness, and carry $\mathcal C_X$ to $\mathcal C_Y$. If all finite reductions of $K$ have cohomology in an integer interval $[a,b]$, the same interval works for all reductions of $g_R^*K$. Neither coefficient category is replaced by modules over the constant $R$-sheaf.

proof.text: Use finite-type preservation over the Noetherian field spectrum and quasi-compactness to make X and Z Noetherian. The open embedding induces a Noetherian topology on U and U is locally Noetherian. Infer quasi-separatedness and quasi-compactness. The finite field cardinality gives characteristic p; l≠p gives a unit in the field and hence in every structure stalk.

Extract the extension-ring part of standard_quotients_perfect, retaining the actual complex, its free terms, augmentation, differential and finiteness. Invertibility of the localized augmentation gives QuasiIso. Evaluate its degree-zero identity on sections.

The legacy global completeness predicate quantifies over FiniteFieldDatum in universe zero. Nat.exists_infinite_primes (l+1) supplies a prime p>l. The field ZMod p and its algebraic closure define such a datum with a=1, q=p, and p≠l. Apply the published Roos/legacy equivalence with this proof-only auxiliary datum. No data of the coefficient sheaf or pullback functor is changed.

For each immersion obtain the published integral comparison C. The identity round trip transports constructibility to transport(back K). The Roos/legacy completeness equivalence gives completeness of back K. C.gamma is natural. Compose it with the inverse round trip and inverse of the natural strict/reflector comparison to construct gamma, giving precisely its required normalization.

The immersion comparison makes the actual strict completion unit invertible on back K. Whiskering and ordinaryPresentation construct c as asIso of the actual completion transformation. Map the two actualCompletedProjection_compatibility equations under coefficient transport to prove its projection and transition equations.

Apply the two smaller compatibility statements to these already constructed natural isomorphisms. Exact termwise descent makes ordinary triangulated. Transport triangulation and constant-section linearity through c and gamma; their composite commutes with shifts by the general natural-transformation composition and inverse instances.

Choose the common interval supplied by constructibility of transport(back K), apply the immersion theorem, and transport across ordinaryPresentation, c and gamma. For an arbitrary interval with a≤b use the same theorem and reduction homology isomorphisms. If a>b the source support is empty and lies in both [0,0] and [1,1]. The two immersion conclusions force target support empty, proving the requested interval without an extra hypothesis.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q10-e9a75ece4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS: 0-node, 6-step assembly; statement and stmt_deps unchanged; no SGA; the main-20261015 open-closed-triangle integral/rational paragraphs are the route. All six steps check: (1) the geometry hypotheses match (finite type over a Noetherian field; closed immersion is proper; open subscheme; locally Noetherian ⇒ quasi-separated; qcqs permanence makes j quasi-compact). (2) O_E is a DVR with finite residue field; [O_E -ϖ^n-> O_E]; profinite-coefficient inverse image keeps constants, projections and transitions. (3) lem-sf-immersion-completed-pullback-comparison applies to i and j as locally closed immersions and gives c_g, exactness, preservation of completeness and the same uniform interval. (4) lem-a1-integral-pullback-completed-comparison: ℓ is invertible over char p; the integral level of def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom is literally def-pur-integral-derived-operations, the a1 integral functor; it gives γ_g with projection and shift equations; transitions follow from the derived-limit projections. (5) The augmentation (0,x) is fixed by the Roos shift ((-1)^r y,x) for every r; the hypotheses of the exact-product strict-limit lemma come from immersion-limit-preservation (c is an iso) and countable-products-exact. (6) R-linearity by conjugation, triangles transported, reductions and interval transferred. Edge cases (empty Z/U, zero K, negative shifts, n=1,2) are fine. Advisory: pre-existing unsplit lem-sf-integral-ordinary-recollement-realization contains the pullback-comparison clause inside a larger package; this overlap is not a new restatement. Batch-5 flag: lem-a1-finite-pullback-strict-tower-comparison → lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact (sk-i-curve-zero) is the generic fact that inverse image of a geometric morphism is exact. It is not given by and not a step of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so accepted. tool_uses accepted.

lean.statement: theorem integralImmersionPullbackNormalization (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (_hl : l ≠ D.p) (X U Z : Scheme.{u}) (aX : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k)) [IsSeparated aX] [LocallyOfFiniteType aX] [QuasiCompact aX] (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] (_hcomplement : Set.range j = (Set.range i)ᶜ) : IsNoetherian X ∧ IsNoetherian U ∧ IsNoetherian Z ∧ QuasiSeparatedSpace X ∧ QuasiSeparatedSpace U ∧ QuasiSeparatedSpace Z ∧ QuasiCompact j ∧ FinitePerfectQuotients l E ∧ Nonempty (Comparison l E i) ∧ Nonempty (Comparison l E j)
lean.note: The three functors are compared over the recorded completed coefficient sheaves using the existing finite-projection-normalized coefficient transport. Comparison fixes gamma by the integral strict-projection comparison and c by the actual strict quotient unit. It retains finite projections, transitions, canonical shifts, exactness, constant-section R-linearity, constructibility and the unchanged reduction interval. Helpers belong to this normalization; moduleRoundTrip_exists is uniquely fixed on sections. Existing data are publicly reexported from IntegralImmersionPullbackNormalizationData.
